issues.legal_issue: A statutory exclusion of a protected tenant’s rights and privileges does not remove the landlord’s right to terminate the tenancy, but removes the tenant’s corresponding protection against termination of the whole leased land.
material_facts: The landlord terminated the protected tenancy for personal cultivation and obtained possession of the land.
The tenant’s recorded ownership of additional land met the statutory threshold that excluded him from rights and privileges under the relevant tenant-protection provisions.
The tenant had initially been allowed to retain half the leased land, but the exclusion was relied on to award the landlord possession of the entire land.
issues.conclusion: The exclusion deprived the tenant of the right to retain half the leased land, while the landlord’s right to terminate arose independently; the landlord could therefore obtain possession of the entire leased land.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 34(1) and 34(2-A) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, a landlord could terminate a protected tenancy for bona fide personal cultivation, subject to the tenant’s right to retain half the leased land. Section 88(1A) removed the tenant’s rights and privileges under sections 32 and 34, including that right of retention, but did not itself confer the landlord’s termination right or do more than withdraw the tenant’s protections. The Court approved Janga Baoji Mali v. Nasarat Jahan Begum, which held that a landlord who establishes a case under section 34(1) is not restricted by protections under sections 34(2) and 34(2-A) when those protections are unavailable to the tenant.

predicates.protected_tenancy_termination: A landlord terminated a protected tenancy after giving notice that the land was bona fide required for personal cultivation.
predicates.tenant_met_disqualifying_ownership_thres: The tenant’s recorded ownership of additional land met the threshold that made the tenant ineligible for the relevant tenant protections.
predicates.landlord_entitled_to_entire_leased_land: The landlord may obtain possession of the entire leased land.

issues.definition: When a landlord terminates a protected tenancy for personal cultivation and the tenant meets the disqualifying ownership threshold, the landlord may obtain the entire leased land.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord who obtains land after terminating a tenancy must restore it if the landlord fails to use it for the stated purpose or ceases that use within the prescribed period, and a transferee’s possession is not treated as the landlord’s possession.
material_facts: After the tenancy was terminated, the landlord obtained possession of the land for personal cultivation.
Before the prescribed period had expired, the landlord sold the land to another person and transferred possession to that person.
The tenant’s successor applied for restoration of possession, and the Court held that the transferee’s possession could not be regarded as the landlord’s possession.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s transfer of the land and possession meant that the landlord ceased to use it for the stated purpose within the prescribed period, so the former tenant’s successors were entitled to restoration of possession, subject to legal limits on their holding.
issues.legal_principle: Section 37(1) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, applies after possession has been obtained following termination under section 34. It requires restoration to the former tenant if the landlord fails to use the land for the purpose stated in the notice within the initial period, or ceases that use within the later prescribed period. The transferee’s possession cannot be treated as the landlord’s possession.

predicates.restoration_proceeding_after_tenancy_ter: A former tenant or successor sought restoration after a landlord obtained possession following termination of the tenancy.
predicates.landlord_took_possession_for_stated_purp: The landlord obtained possession for the purpose stated in the termination notice.
predicates.landlord_failed_to_use_land_for_stated_p: The landlord did not use the land for the stated purpose within the applicable initial period.
predicates.landlord_ceased_that_use: The landlord stopped using the land for the stated purpose within the applicable later period.
predicates.landlord_transferred_land_and_possession: The landlord transferred the land and possession to another person.
predicates.former_tenant_entitled_to_restoration: The former tenant or successor is entitled to restoration of possession, subject to legal limits on the holding.

issues.definition: When a restoration proceeding follows a tenancy termination and the landlord, having taken possession for the stated purpose, fails to use or ceases to use the land for that purpose and transfers the land and possession to another, the former tenant or successor is entitled to restoration.
